entries.name: Riveted Ironstem
entries.notes: A SET IS ALL REFERENCE AND NO INVENTION. Four kinds of reference appear here and every one of them resolves against a frozen registry or a frozen wave. THE CAPABILITY SITS AT THE LOWEST THRESHOLD, and this inverts genre convention deliberately. Diablo 3 put the payoff at the 6-piece, every build became 'the set', and Diablo 4 abandoned sets almost entirely. Here the 2-piece grants the thing rares cannot roll and the higher thresholds grant plain numbers, so a two-piece splash is always worth taking and running two half-sets is a real build rather than a worse version of committing to one. THIS IS NOT ADVICE — a set whose capability is not at its lowest threshold FAILS IMPORT. A capability is an atom of a non-stat kind. `atom.retribution` is `resource.delta` on OnDamageTaken — the thing that hits you takes it back, which is what a chassis wrapped in thorns should do. Every HIGHER threshold is `stat.modify` / `stat.derived` only, and none of them may use a `More`-op family: `atom.bulwark` and `atom.savagery` are the two `More` families and both would reject as SetTierForbiddenAtom. atom.vitality (Flat), atom.fortitude (Increased) and atom.might (Flat) are all safe. `Increased` sums with every other Increased on the actor, so a set built from it is self-diminishing as the rest of the build grows — that is diminishing returns from compose rules that already exist, not a bolt-on curve. MEMBERS ARE ROLES, AND TWO ROLES ARE FORBIDDEN. All four member roles are frame-neutral role ids from core.v1.json, and each must be in the HYBRID ROLE CORE. Two of the fifteen are not: `ward-array` and `jewel-minor-b` both carry hybridEligible=false, so naming either as a member fails SetRoleNotUniversal at load and — because import is all-or-nothing — takes the whole batch down with it. This is the single easiest way to write a set that cannot import. A set may also claim AT MOST ONE of armament-primary / armament-secondary: weapons are where build identity lives, and a set owning both owns the build. This one takes the off-hand only. Four members is the pattern (six is the rare 'grand set'), there is ALWAYS a threshold at 2, and the top threshold may not exceed the member count. The members are declared by role, not by base-type id, because the generator resolves each role to the frame-specific member containers — at most one per (role, frame) — which is how one frame-neutral set is completable by a pure humanoid, a pure plant, or a hybrid mixing both. THEME AND NAME. `themeKey` is the `nameKey` of a theme in themes.v1.json, and only 5 of the 13 themes have a set partition at all: thorned-chassis, verdant-graft, rusted-legion, frostbitten-vanguard, sunwoven-almanac. The theme id is not invented and the theme's own `avoid` list is binding on the flavour — thorned-chassis rejects pristine factory-new metal and rejects pure organic growth with no scrap in it. The name is `compound`: `riveted` from themeAdjectivePools['thorned-chassis'], `ironstem` from uniqueSetSeedPools['thorned-chassis']. A seed word is ATOMIC — the normalizer resolves it whole and must never decompose it into iron + stem, or it would collide with names sharing neither idea. `nameKey` is the name slugged, and it is unique across the ENTIRE corpus, not per kind: if a base-type partition had already claimed this slug, the fix is to append this partition's own token, never to pick a near-miss spelling. Every threshold states a `powerBand` and no set states a magnitude; the per-piece value budget is checked downstream from those bands and the member count.
